text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
May 1 is a public and market holiday so newspapers will issue their next edition on Saturday, May 3.
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Passenger and freight rail fares rose by 19 percent and 51 percent respectively starting May 1, due to a recent government decision to introduce a railway tax.
- Prices for gas and for thermal power rose five and three times respectively from May 1, as part of government steps to liberalise energy prices.
- General Motors is looking at projects to upgrade Romanian rolling stock, Transport Minister Traian Basescu said during a visit to the United States.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Romanian economy will revive and foreign investment will rise as a result of the centrist government's reform programme, a survey by the U.S. Congress Research Service shows.
CAPITAL
- The World Bank's resident mission in Romania is expected to decide in May whether to ask the bank's board to release a second tranche of a loan to the country.
General:
ADEVARUL
- Pensioners will get a monthly allowance worth 13,500 lei to compensate for the rise in bread prices, according to a government decision valid until the end of September.
- Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi is expected in Bucharest on May 5 accompanied by a business delegation.
- Romanian chief spy Virgil Magureanu resigned as head of Romanian Intelligence Service and is considering entering politics and joining an un-named centrist party.
- Visiting German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel has avoided expressing his country's support for Romania's early admission into NATO, the newspaper says.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The Romanian diaspora in the United States has started to lobby for Romania's quick NATO integration and will send letters to the White House and the Congress in support.
- NATO will take into account Russia's interests when deciding on allowing in new members at the alliance's July summit in Madrid, Kinkel said.
CAPITAL
- Romania spends 500,000 lei for every litre of blood donated. Some 137,000 litres were donated in 1996.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- A 400-strong Romanian batallion left to join the international peacekeeping mission in Albania. ($=7,085 lei)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
